DUST & HARVEST
Settler's Field Guide & Almanac
Who is Elias?
A man with a deed, a debt, and a plough. Not much else worth counting.
Day 1 — Dry Summer — Week 1
"Got the keys to the place from the bank man. He handed them over without looking me in the eye. I don't know if that means the land is good or bad. I'll find out. Put the hoe in the ground before dark. That felt right."
The Situation

Elias came to the frontier the same way most people did — a deed, a loan, and an idea that hard work would settle the rest. The bank holds the mortgage. Weekly payments start at $500 and climb $200 each week. Miss too many and the land goes back to whoever holds the paper.

The farm is real enough — six patches of tillable dirt, a broken barn, a well, and a river to the south. The wilderness beyond the fence is full of things worth gathering and things worth avoiding.

The Deeper Question

Altaverde Holdings — the company that built and then killed the eastern railroad — holds mineral survey rights on everything within twenty miles of the old rail line. Your farm is almost certainly inside that radius.

The people at the Hobo Camp north of town know more than they let on. Dale spent twelve years as a railroad man. Vera was a city clerk who's seen the paperwork. Simons farmed sixty acres before a void notice made them not his. Dr. Lena came out here for reasons she hasn't shared. Kit is heading east toward the ocean.

Dale — Hobo Camp
"You should look at your deed. Not the copy the bank gave you — the original land registry filing. If the mineral rights are held separately, what you own is the surface. What's underneath still belongs to whoever filed the claim."
The Goal

Pay off the weekly land debt across 24 weeks. Payments increase every week — early weeks are manageable, later ones demand a real operation. Clear the debt and the land is yours.

Debt clock — top-left HUD. Shows balance and days to next payment. Pay at market [M] → Bank tab. Paying ahead reduces future pressure.
Wilt kills. Miss watering before the 8am grace period and a crop wilts — that's your one warning. Miss a second day and the crop dies, the plot resets to bare dirt, and the seeds are gone. Peaceful and Easy difficulty disable wilt entirely.
Debt clock — top-left HUD. Shows balance and days to next payment. Pay at market [M] → Bank tab. Paying ahead reduces future pressure.
Missing a payment doesn't end the game immediately — but unpaid weeks roll over. If the total climbs too high to recover, the frontier wins.
Getting Started
The first week is about survival. The second is about getting ahead. Everything after is planning.
Day One Priorities
🌱
Till and plant
Press F → farm panel. Carrots are fast and cheap. Till [E near dirt], water [E with water can], plant. Refill can at the well.
💰
First sale
Walk east to Town. Press M for market. Sell everything. First payment is $500 due at start of Week 2.
🌿
Gather while you wait
Crops take time. Walk south into Wilderness and chop trees [E] or gather herbs from bushes. Both sell.
🍽
Eat
Hunger drains all day. Press H to eat from hotbar. Keep food there. Cooked meals give far more than raw crops.
HP, Stamina & Hunger

HP — lost to enemies, storms, starvation. Restored by food and potions. Hit zero: lose carried goods, respawn at farm.

Stamina — used for sprinting, gathering, tilling, mining. Regenerates still. Hunger directly affects stamina regen — well-fed gives +25% regen, starving barely recovers.

Hunger — drains through the day. Rate changes by season: Summer ×1.4, Winter brutal ×1.8, Spring easy ×0.8. At 0, HP drains. Keep food on hotbar.

Town Reputation

Every sale builds small town rep. Higher rep = better sell prices: unknown ×0.92, acquaintance standard, trusted +10%, revered +20%. Check tier in Stats.

Farming
The farm is your base of income. Everything else is supplementary.
The Cycle

Till → Water → Plant → Water daily → Harvest. Crops not watered before the 8am grace period begin wilting. A wilted crop is a warning — water it that same day or it dies overnight and the plot resets to bare dirt. Each dawn your water can refills automatically.

Wilt = one warning, then death. Miss the 8am grace period → crop wilts. Miss a second day → crop dies, plot resets to bare dirt, seeds lost. No recovery. Peaceful and Easy modes disable wilt entirely.

Cooking

Buy Cooking Campfire from market (Upgrades → Farm, $120). Best early investment. Cooked meals sell for far more than raw ingredients and restore substantial hunger. Requires 1 coal per recipe as fuel.

Best early loop: Potatoes + cow milk → Potato Mash (+60 stamina). Sell surplus, eat the rest during long mining sessions.
Animals

Buy from Livestock tab in market. Fill trough with hay or animals produce nothing. Barn Repair ($500) shelters animals from wolves. Fence Lanterns ($160) deter night attacks. Both essential before Winter.

The Seasons
Forty days make a full cycle. Each season changes what grows, how hungry you get, storm frequency, and what the market pays.
☀️
Dry Summer — 10 days
Hunger drains ×1.4. Dust storms common. Summer crops peak. Glowroot/moonshroom struggle. Market pays more for melon, pepper.
🍂
Harvest Fall — 10 days
Hunger normal. Crops grow 30% faster overall. Enemies 20% more active. Pumpkin, corn, dustwheat, blueberry all peak.
❄️
Cold Winter — 10 days
Hunger drains ×1.8. Storms constant. Enemies +50% active. Most summer crops banned. Glowroot and moonshroom thrive. Stock up before it arrives.
🌧️
Wet Spring — 10 days
Hunger eases ×0.8. Rain waters 65% of crops at dawn automatically. Crops grow 50% faster. Enemies least active. Best planting window.

Winter checklist: stock cooked meals · harvest all summer crops · plant glowroot in fall · repair the barn · buy fence lanterns.
The World
The frontier is larger than the farm. Each zone has its own rules.
🌾 The Farm
Home. Six tillable patches, well, barn, campfire, forge, workbench. The chest stores overflow. Safe at night — enemies don't cross the fence.
🏘 Town
East across the road. Market [M] — sell goods, buy seeds, upgrades, livestock, contracts, pay the bank. Maya gives market tips. Rex manages contracts. Always safe.
🌵 Wilderness
South of the river. Trees, rocks, herbs to gather. Enemies spawn at night. Mine entrance is here. Dangerous at night. Random encounters happen here.

🎣 Three fishing spots line the river bank. Hold [E] near the water with a rod — cast, then press [E] again when the BITE prompt flashes. Dawn and dusk pull more rare fish. Drop a crop in your inventory to use as bait automatically.
⛏ The Mine
Three floors — copper, iron, gold, crystal. Deeper = darker and more dangerous. Open 6am–8pm only. Hazards: gas pockets and cave-ins. Bring a lantern upgrade. Smelt ore into bars for +80% value.
🏜 The Badlands
Far west. Combat zone with a Heat system — more kills = harder enemies but better loot. Outpost has a vendor and bounty board. Heat resets when you leave.
🏕 Hobo Camp
North of town. Five characters with history. Talk to all of them — some know things about Altaverde that matter. The camp creek holds rare fishing finds: Deed Fragments and Surveyor's Compasses.
⚓ The Ocean Dock
Maren runs the dock. Deep-sea fishing from a boat catches the most valuable fish. Pirate skiffs attack at night. Ocean cooking recipes (salt chowder, swordfish steak) sell for serious money.

🎣 Fishing mechanics: Cast with [E] near water, then watch for the BITE prompt and press [E] again to hook it. Dawn and dusk catch more rare fish. Use crops as bait — corn attracts catfish, glowroot pulls rare species. Upgrade your rod at the market for faster casts and better rare rates. Check your Fishing Logbook in the Stats screen to track every species caught.
Fishing
Three zones, 30+ species, one rod and a lot of patience. Or a better rod and less patience.
How it works

Stand near water with a Fishing Rod in your inventory. Press [E] to cast. After the line lands, wait — when the !! BITE message flashes, press [E] again immediately to hook it. Miss the window and the fish gets away. The window is short on a bamboo rod and longer on upgraded ones.

Dawn (5–7am) and dusk (6–8pm) are peak fishing hours — rare fish are more likely during these windows. Winter slows the river; Wet Spring is the best season to fish.
Bait

Carry crops in your inventory and the game uses one automatically as bait when you cast. Different crops attract different fish:

BaitAttractsBonus
🌽 CornCatfish, Bass, Turtle×2.2
🥔 PotatoPerch, Common Fish×1.8
🫐 BlueberrySunfish, Golden Fish×2.5
✨ GlowrootGolden Fish, Turtle×3.0
🥕 CarrotCommon, Perch, Catfish×1.6

Bait is only consumed if you successfully land the catch — miss the bite window and it stays in your bag.

Rod upgrades

Buy rod upgrades at Market → Upgrades → Tools. Each tier reduces cast time and improves rare catch rates.

RodCostCast timeRare rate
🎣 Bamboo Rod$80BaseBase
🎣 Cane Rod$180−12%×1.2
🎣 Copper-Tip$420−25%×1.5
🎣 Iron Split-Cane$900−38%×1.9
🎣 Gold-Inlaid$2200−50%×2.5
Where to fish
🌊 River (Wilderness)
Three spots along the south bank. Basic table — perch, catfish, bass, common fish. Snapper Turtle and Golden Fish are the rare prizes. Junk Boot odds are higher than you'd like.
🏞 Hobo Camp Creek
Murky frontier runoff. Crawdad, mudcat, scraggly fish. Higher junk rate but rare finds include the Deed Fragment and Surveyor's Compass — both useful for Vera's case.
⚓ Ocean Dock
Shallow dock access from day one. Deep water requires a Schooner or better (or trusted Ocean rep with a Sloop). Deep table has swordfish, bluefin tuna, giant grouper, deepwater pearls, and kraken ink. Night fishing skews rarer. Boat tier also speeds up cast time.
Cooking fish

Most fish sell raw, but cooking adds significant value. Stand at the campfire with fish + coal in your inventory and press [E] — it'll offer a quick-cook shortcut if a recipe is ready. Full recipe list is in Market → Crafting → Campfire Cooking.

Check the Fishing Logbook in the Stats screen (press [Tab] or open the stats overlay) to track every species you've caught across all three zones. First catch of any species shows a special message.
The Badlands & Heat
The Badlands rewards aggression. The longer you fight, the more it pays — and the harder it hits back.
Heat System

Every kill raises Heat (0–100). Heat determines spawn rate, enemy damage, and loot quality. Resets on exit — every run starts fresh.

CALM
Heat 0–19. Standard. Learn the layout, find the outpost.
Loot ×1.0
WANTED
Heat 20–44. Spawns +30%. Blood Dust starts dropping.
Loot ×1.25
INFAMOUS
Heat 45–69. Spawns +65%. Wanted Posters drop. Think about leaving.
Loot ×1.6
OUTLAW
Heat 70–89. Double spawn rate. +50% damage. Outlaw Crowns can drop.
Loot ×2.1
LEGEND
Heat 90–100. ×2.8 spawns. +80% damage. Legend Shards — rarest drop in the game.
Loot ×3.0
Enemies
🐍
Rattler +3 heat
Fast, venomous. Carry Rosehip Tonic or Fever Root.
🦅
Vulture +4 heat
Airborne, circles before diving. Feathers sell well.
🦂
Dust Scorpion +5
Slow but heavy hits. Stinger is worth good money.
🤠
Outlaw +6 heat
Armed. Drops bandit scarves. Find near ruins.
🌪️
Dust Devil +7
Erratic. Hard to hit. Drops Dust Devil Eye at high heat.
💀
Desperado +18
Rare elite. $350 bounty. Do not engage unprepared.
Tip: Enter with full HP and a poultice. Use the outpost as a reset point. Exit portal pulses green on the east edge — or find the SE portal bottom-right.
Economy & Markets
Prices move. Some days a carrot is worth $8, some days $14. Pay attention to the trend arrows.
How Prices Work

Every item fluctuates daily based on volatility, seasonal bonuses, and market events. The market shows current price and a trend arrow (▲▼—). Rare items like Glowroot and Swordfish Steak swing wildly. Staples like Carrot are more stable.

Key Market Events
🌵
Drought
All food prices surge. Sell your stockpile.
⛏
Mine Collapse
Stone, coal, and ore spike sharply.
🎪
Frontier Feast
All cooked goods worth double. Best event for cooks.
❄
Deep Frost
Potato and carrot worth double. Summer crops worthless.
🐺
Livestock Fair
Eggs, wool, and milk worth nearly double.
🚢
Shipwreck
Wood and plank prices double. Good time to chop.
Contracts

Talk to Rex east of the market or use the Contracts tab. Each contract asks for a specific quantity within a deadline at above-market rates. Completing streaks pays a bonus. Don't accept what you can't deliver.

The Debt Schedule

Week 1: $500 · Week 2: $700 · Week 3: $900 · and so on, +$200 per week. Pay at Market → Bank tab. Paying ahead reduces future pressure. The debt clock never pauses — pay before long expeditions.

Mine Forge upgrade — raw ore smelted into bars sells for ~80% more. 3 copper ore → 1 copper bar. Worth the stamina cost every time.
